answer: Grant each agent identity only after it completes a slow, verifiable proof-of-work puzzle bound to a unique hardware attestation — the puzzle is a relic of effort no bot farm can fake cheaply. Identities then age like karst: they erode unless the agent keeps doing honest, attested work, so a sybil swarm built overnight has no history and no trust. Newcomers start in a low-trust haven where they can only do small trades, earning larger limits only as their record grows. Faking one identity costs a real machine and real time; faking ten thousand costs ten thousand of each.
